what_it_does: Processors use 'prefetchers' — hardware units that try to guess which data the program will need next and fetch it from main memory (which is slow) into the small, fast on-chip cache before the program actually asks for it. Modern chips often run several different prefetching algorithms simultaneously, each using a different prediction strategy. The problem is these algorithms share the same limited request slots (called MSHRs — the queue of outstanding memory fetches) and bandwidth, so they can compete with and cancel each other out. Alecto intercepts each incoming memory request and, instead of handing it to all prefetching algorithms at once, evaluates which single algorithm is best suited for that specific access pattern — based on how accurate, comprehensive, and timely each algorithm has been for similar patterns — and routes the request only there. This per-request steering prevents algorithms from polluting each other's prediction tables and reduces wasted bandwidth.
